appraisal_events.evidence: l'homme que vous « adorez »... est le plus grand imbécile que la terre ait jamais porté... c'est tout de même un fameux culot de la part d'un homme dont l'arrière-grand-père était un petit fermier... Il va à peine au Jockey, tant il y est gêné, ce prétendu prince.
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup dismantles the capitaine's standing on several fronts at once: he is called an imbecile, exposed as a snob who despises a genuinely admirable subordinate, and mocked as a jumped-up Napoleonic parvenu ill at ease among the old aristocracy.

appraisal_events.evidence: ces traits caractéristiques des Guermantes, de cette race restée si particulière au milieu du monde... elle reste isolée dans sa gloire divinement ornithologique, car elle semble issue... de l'union d'une déesse et d'un oiseau.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator raptly mythologizes the Guermantes lineage embodied in the duchesse's features, and Robert, whom he observes resembling his aunt's photograph, gains reflected prestige from that visible kinship.

status_effects.explanation: Called the greatest imbecile alive and shown to be narrow and obsessed with trivial military minutiae, his personal standing is sharply lowered.

His claim to princely rank is undercut by his humble Napoleonic ancestry and his visible unease at the Jockey Club, marking him as not fully accepted by the old aristocracy he tries to look down on others from.
The narrator elevates her, through the family traits she shares with Robert, to an almost mythic, divine plane.
Robert benefits from prestige by association, as the narrator admires in him the same rare Guermantes features he prizes in the duchesse.

ambiguities: The narrator closes Saint-Loup's tirade against the capitaine by noting it unconsciously mixes democratic ideals with inherited aristocratic prejudice against Napoleonic nobility, which tempers how fully the diminishment of the capitaine should be taken as an objective or narrator-endorsed judgment rather than Saint-Loup's own unwitting bias.
